label: scenario
evidence: In commit 9d90e40264668cf41ec83c922bd8a10def27b546, any RUN_COMMAND_DENIED event was treated as a permanent terminal blocker in RunService.resume. When Codex automated approval reviews failed due to usage limits, runs were permanently wedged. The fix introduced --retry-approval to validate and acknowledge specific usage-limit denial artifacts, ignoring them during resume blocker checks while still requiring fresh native approval.
cue: When automated external provider evaluation or approval review rejections (such as quota exhaustion or usage limits) are treated as terminal command denials that permanently block run recovery.
check: Can transient or rate-limited provider review failures be distinguished from intentional policy denials and explicitly retried on resume, while preserving artifact audit integrity and requiring fresh authorization?
